name: Universal Mental Factors
intro: The Abhidhamma's map of the mind: seven factors present in every single moment of consciousness. Four you already know — phassa, vedanā, saññā, ekaggatā — and three that complete the set.

words.gloss: volition; the intending that organises a mind-moment

etymology.note: the factor the Buddha equates with kamma — the leaning of the mind that makes an action an action

canonicalLine.translation: it is volition, monks, that I call kamma

words.gloss: life faculty; what keeps a mind-moment alive for its duration

etymology.note: not the body's vitality but the mental one — the factor that sustains its co-arising factors until they cease

words.gloss: attention; turning the mind toward an object

etymology.root: manasi (in the mind, locative of manas) + kāra (making)
etymology.note: the steering — yoniso manasikāra, wise attention, is the same factor pointed well

talk.text: Every moment of mind, the Abhidhamma says, carries seven factors whether we notice or not.
leans toward it — this is where kamma is made.
holds the mind on it for that instant,
keeps the whole moment alive, and
is the turning-toward that chose this object rather than another.

suttaRec.title: Nibbedhika — Penetrative
suttaRec.blurb: The sutta where the Buddha defines kamma as cetanā — intention — and lays out what must be understood about sense pleasures, feelings, and the taints.
